themes_detail.label: Encampment Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints in Midtown surged to 228 THIS WEEK, up 51% from the 8-week baseline average of 151.2 weekly complaints, signaling a sharp deterioration in street homelessness across the district in real time.
evidence: 228 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 151.2 average weekly baseline (z-score: 4.02, severity: high)
Encampment is largest single complaint category over 90 days with 2,100 total complaints
Spike is most recent and statistically significant signal in dataset
reporting_angles: Map and visit the clusters of new encampments reported this week; interview residents and outreach workers about what triggered the surge
Investigate city's encampment response capacity and whether intake/shelter availability has bottlenecked

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Obstruction Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints jumped 187% to 28 LAST WEEK from a 9.8 weekly average, indicating rapid deterioration of pedestrian access across Midtown as vendors, construction materials, or debris increasingly block sidewalks.
evidence: 28 obstruction complaints LAST WEEK vs. 9.8 weekly baseline average (z-score: 5.34, severity: high)
187% spike represents sustained deviation from normal
Converges with elevated mobile food vendor complaints (96% spike) suggesting vendor-related obstructions
reporting_angles: Document which blocks/intersections have the worst obstruction problems; photograph before/after city response
Interview pedestrians and retailers about impact on foot traffic and accessibility

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints spiked 96% to 23 complaints THREE WEEKS AGO from an 11.8 weekly average, reflecting ongoing friction over vendor density, cart placement, or permit compliance in Midtown's high-foot-traffic corridors.
evidence: 23 mobile food vendor complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 11.8 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.86, severity: high)
Converges with obstruction spike, suggesting vendors are blocking sidewalks or crowding commercial corridors
Cannabis retailer complaints also up 243%, indicating broader enforcement/compliance issues with street-level retail
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors and department of consumer affairs about compliance burden and permit bottlenecks
Canvass Times Square, Herald Square, and other high-vendor-density zones to determine root of complaints

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped 208% to 20 complaints TWO WEEKS AGO from a 6.5 weekly average, indicating emerging quality-of-life concerns in Midtown's public parks as weather improves or event activity increases.
evidence: 20 park noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 6.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.46, severity: high)
Part of broader noise escalation (street/sidewalk noise also elevated)
Likely seasonal or event-driven; worth investigating specific parks and sources
reporting_angles: Identify which parks (Bryant Park, Madison Square Park, etc.) generated the most complaints and why
Interview parks department about event scheduling and enforcement capacity

themes_detail.label: Infrastructure Deterioration: Flooring & Stairs
themes_detail.summary: Flooring and stair complaints spiked 540% to 4 complaints THREE WEEKS AGO from a 0.6 weekly baseline, a sharp outlier suggesting emerging hazards in Midtown buildings or public infrastructure that warrant investigation.
evidence: 4 flooring/stairs complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.85, severity: high)
Baseline is so low that even small absolute spike registers as extreme percentage increase
3,830 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (mostly alterations: 3,471) suggests active construction that may be damaging building infrastructure
reporting_angles: Cross-reference flooring/stair complaints with active DOB permit locations to see if construction is causing collateral damage
Investigate which buildings or public spaces generated these complaints and assess structural risk
